summary: The motion rules, each shown as what not to do and what Picasso does. The reasoning in full is in docs/foundations/motion-before-and-after.md.

pairs.dont: Count a number up, or draw a chart in.
pairs.why: Someone is trying to read it. A number that is still climbing cannot be read, and on a console a value that moves looks like a value that is changing.

pairs.dont: Close on a curve that starts slowly.
pairs.do: Decelerate both ways, and leave on the shorter step.
pairs.why: The first frames after a click are the ones people watch. An ease-in holds them back, so the dialog seems to hesitate before it goes.

pairs.dont: Scale a surface up from zero.
pairs.why: Nothing real appears from a point. From zero, the eye follows a panel flying outwards; from 96%, it sees a panel arrive.

pairs.dont: Grow a menu from its own centre.
pairs.do: Grow it from the control that opened it.
pairs.why: A menu belongs to its button. From its centre it appears beside the button; from the trigger's corner it comes out of it, and that is what says where it came from.

pairs.dont: Give a drawer half a second each way.
pairs.do: Slide in over 300ms and out over 200.
pairs.why: A drawer is opened dozens of times in a shift. Half a second each way is a second of waiting for every look; the sheet curve covers most of the distance in the first third, so 300 feels immediate.

pairs.dont: Animate a width, a height or a position.
pairs.do: Change layout at once. Animate transform and opacity only.
pairs.why: A width that animates re-lays out everything beside it on every frame, and beside the rail is a page of charts. The count under each example is how many times the page changed size.

pairs.dont: Grow a control when the pointer is over it.
pairs.do: Leave hover to colour, and give 3% under a press.
pairs.why: Hover is not a decision: the pointer crosses a dozen controls on its way somewhere. A press is, and a control that gives a little under it is the interface saying it heard.

pairs.dont: Switch animation off under reduced motion.
pairs.do: Replace the travel with a short fade.
pairs.why: Reduced motion asks for less movement, not less information. A drawer that is simply there, with nothing connecting it to what opened it, is harder to follow than one that fades in where it will sit.
